cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses, Israel's leader, a message for the sons of Aaron, Moses's brother. Aaron's sons are the priests, and these rules are just for them. Tighten your apron strings, friend.

cards.question: The first rule for the priests is about death. True or false: A priest may defile himself for any dead person among his people.

cards.text: But there's an exception for his immediate family: his mother, father, son, daughter or brother. Your second cousin? Sorry, cuz.

cards.question: One more relative makes the priest's exception list. Who is it?
True or false: A priest may defile himself for those related to him by marriage.

cards.text: Next up: how a priest looks. Priests must not make bald spots on their heads or shave off the edges of their beards, and friend, as a stamper with THIS mustache, I read that verse and felt SEEN.

cards.question: There's a third thing the priests must not do to their own bodies. What is it?
God says the priests must be holy to Him and not profane His name. Why?

answers.text: They present the LORD's food offerings
They were born first in their families

cards.text: Then it gets personal: who a priest can marry. He must not marry a woman defiled by prostitution or divorced by her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.

cards.question: True or false: God says the priest is to be regarded as holy, because the LORD is holy.

cards.text: If a priest's daughter defiles herself by prostituting herself, she profanes her father, and she must be burned in the fire. The text doesn't soften that one, friend, and I won't either.
Now comes the priest who is highest among his brothers, the one with the anointing oil poured on his head. He must not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.

cards.question: Regular priests could defile themselves for close family. True or false: The highest priest may defile himself for his father or mother.
The highest priest must not leave or desecrate the sanctuary of his God. Why not?

answers.text: The anointing oil of his God is on him
He keeps watch over the gold inside
The people need him at the gate

cards.text: Then it's back to marriage, and the highest priest gets the EXTENDED edition of the list. The woman he marries must be a virgin.

cards.question: The highest priest is not to marry a ___, a divorced woman, or one defiled by prostitution.
The highest priest is to marry a virgin from his own people. Why?

answers.text: So he does not defile his offspring
So his wife can serve beside him
So his family keeps its land

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses another message for Aaron himself, and this one is for the generations to come. Friend, the warranty cards in my old junk drawer couldn't last ONE year, and this rule is already booked for the GREAT-GREAT-GRANDKIDS.

cards.question: For the generations to come, which of Aaron's descendants may not approach to offer the food of his God?

answers.text: Any who has a physical defect
Any who was born outside Israel

cards.text: Then God lists the defects one by one, like being blind or lame, or having a broken foot or hand. A descendant of Aaron who has a defect is not to come near to offer the food of his God.

cards.question: A descendant of Aaron with a defect can't offer the food of his God. True or false: He may still eat the holy food of his God.
Because he has a defect, a descendant of Aaron must not go near the ___ or approach the ___.
Why must a priest with a defect not go near the veil or approach the altar?

answers.text: To keep the altar fire burning
To give him rest from his work

cards.question: Moses passes along everything the LORD said about the priests. Who does he tell?

answers.text: Aaron and his sons and all Israel

cards.text: Keep that apron ON, friend, because this teaching on holiness isn't done. The last time I took my apron off mid-batch, I spent TEN MINUTES picking chocolate chips out of my mustache. Don't ask.

findings.problem: "These rules are just for them" goes against the text. In Leviticus 21:8 God speaks to the people ('You are to regard him as holy... He shall be holy to you'), and in 21:24 Moses tells all the Israelites. The line also points the baker toward the wrong answer 'Only Aaron and his sons' on stop 2, card 7.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card says Aaron is Moses's brother. That fact comes from outside the passage (Exodus 4:14), and the card gives no reference for it. The card's "verses" field can only hold the range it tells (Leviticus 21:1), so there's no place to put Exodus 4:14.
findings.question: When a story card states a fact from outside the passage, such as who a new person is, where does its reference go? The "verses" field only covers the passage verses the card tells. Should the reference go in the card text, should the card include an outside reference in its citation, or should the card only use descriptions from inside the passage?

findings.problem: The right answers, veil and altar, are parts of the sanctuary. The wrong answers, camp, well and river, are outdoor places and features. Because they aren't the same kind of thing, the right answers stand out and the card turns into a giveaway instead of a reasoned pick. Better wrong answers would be other sanctuary items the passage doesn't bar him from, like lampstand or basin.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question calls the man 'a priest with a defect.' The text calls him a descendant of Aaron who has a defect (Leviticus 21:21, 23), and he is barred from priestly service. Card 5 uses the text's term, 'a descendant of Aaron.' This card should too.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't follow. Taking off an apron mid-batch wouldn't leave chocolate chips in his mustache, because an apron protects clothes, not a mustache. The cause and the punchline don't connect, so a baker is left asking 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
